messages:
maria: quick heads up — eu telemetry counters are ~6h behind for a small subset of tenants, looks like late KV writes from edge nodes. planning a targeted recompute for 3 tenants to catch up. can we discuss window, concurrency, and customer communication?
kevin: thanks — do we know if this is replay-safe (dup keys)? any dedupe needed on the replayer?
sanjay: logs show duplicate partial batches from the ingest proxy. replayer needs idempotency check + last-write-wins dedupe per key. i can add a fast-path dedupe flag to the run script.
maria: ok; prefer fast-path dedupe over forcing full dedupe (cost).
kevin: agree. UX question: should we run via console or internal API? console has preview cost but API is scriptable for ops.
olivia: FYI customer-success: two of the affected tenants are in onboarding trials, want heads up before we touch their historical counts. we should post a short status + expected duration.
sanjay: proposal: run a canary on tenant "acme-eu" (30m window) with concurrency=12, dedupe=true. if canary looks good, expand to the other 2 tenants with concurrency=24 but throttle to keep latency SLOs.
maria: sounds reasonable. what about routing — do we pin to dedicated capacity or use on-demand GPU pool?
kevin: use dedicated pool for the canary (predictable latency), then switch to on-demand for the wider run if we need to ramp. also enable automatic fallback if queue depth > 2000.
replay-bot: /replay check acme-eu --window 30m --dry-run -> estimated tokens: 2.1M, est cost: $12.40, est time: 18m
maria: perfect, cost estimate looks fine. can we also add a small dashboard panel for progress + kv-dedupe-rate? ops asked for a live trace.
sanjay: i'll add a single-card panel to the backfill dashboard and emit a metric `replay.dedupe_ratio` and `replay.tokens_processed` every 10s.
olivia: i'll draft the customer note: ETA per tenant and link to console progress.
kevin: one internal API change debate: add a top-level `urgency` flag to /replay that affects queue priority vs quotas. for this run i'd like a local override flag instead of a global API change.
maria: agree — don't change API surface for this emergency. add `--priority-bump` to the ops CLI which maps to an internal header for the scheduler. we can RFC the API change later.
sanjay: implemented dedupe fast-path in branch `replay/dedupe-fastpath`, will open PR now. ops CLI will accept `--priority-bump` and set header `x-replay-priority: bump`.
maria: action items: (1) sanjay -> PR + dashboard metric (2) kevin -> allocate dedicated slot for canary and set fallback policy (3) olivia -> send customer note before we start (4) maria -> run canary and post results here. target start in 30m.
kevin: ping me when you start, i'll watch SLO graphs.
olivia: i put the draft in #customer-comms for review.
sanjay: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/replay/pull/1427 — includes dedupe and metric emit.
maria: starting canary now (/replay run --tenant=acme-eu --window=30m --concurrency=12 --dedupe --ops-priority). will post progress updates.
replay-bot: canary started: run_id=rb-202553-1, expected finish 00:18:42, metrics endpoint /metrics/replay/rb-202553-1
kevin: looks green so far, dedupe ratio ~0.06, latency within SLOs.
maria: canary finished: processed 2.05M tokens, dedupe_ratio=0.059, no regressions seen. expanding to the remaining tenants with concurrency=20 and throttle burst 1.5x.
olivia: notified customers: message sent, included console link and expected completion window.
maria: expansion started. assigning followups: sanjay -> watch dedupe alerts; kevin -> monitor SLO + fallback triggers; olivia -> post completion note.
kevin: thanks all — good coordination.
__notes: This thread documents a targeted telemetry recompute for late KV writes in EU region, including ops decisions, small internal-API/CLI debate, cost estimates, and dashboard/metric actions.
